subject: Biochemistry
vignette: A 57-year-old man with a long history of alcohol use disorder is brought in by his sister because of a 6-week decline in memory. He repeatedly invents detailed stories about events that never occurred and cannot recall the name of the hospital or today's date, although he converses fluently. Examination shows horizontal nystagmus, wide-based gait, and a positive Romberg sign. MRI demonstrates atrophy of the mammillary bodies.
question: Which of the following structures is most likely also affected in this patient?

options.text: Medial dorsal nucleus of the thalamus

explanation_correct: This patient has Korsakoff syndrome, the chronic amnestic phase of thiamine deficiency characterized by confabulation, personality change, and permanent loss of memory. The lesions of Wernicke-Korsakoff syndrome involve the mammillary bodies and the medial dorsal nucleus of the thalamus, which explains why the amnesia persists even after acute Wernicke encephalopathy is treated. Thiamine pyrophosphate is required for pyruvate dehydrogenase, alpha-ketoglutarate dehydrogenase, branched-chain ketoacid dehydrogenase, and transketolase, so thiamine deficiency depletes ATP in highly aerobic brain tissue.

explanation_incorrect.A: The caudate nucleus is the site of degeneration in Huntington disease and is not the classic lesion of Wernicke-Korsakoff syndrome.
explanation_incorrect.C: Loss of pigmented dopaminergic neurons in the substantia nigra pars compacta produces Parkinson disease, not confabulation with mammillary body atrophy.
explanation_incorrect.D: The dentate nucleus is a cerebellar relay for motor coordination; cerebellar damage would not produce the amnestic-confabulatory syndrome described.
explanation_incorrect.E: The hippocampus is central to memory formation in Alzheimer disease and other dementias, but the mammillary body-medial dorsal thalamic circuit is the lesion of Korsakoff syndrome.

educationalObjective: Korsakoff syndrome from thiamine deficiency is caused by damage to the mammillary bodies and the medial dorsal nucleus of the thalamus.
